title_en: Ding v. Ji et al. — dispute over liability of educational institution
keywords_en: civil; dispute over liability of educational institution; first instance; basic people's court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Tort Liability Law; whether the educational institution fulfilled its management duties; liability for harm caused by a person without civil capacity; relationship between guardian liability and educational institution liability; partially upheld; dance training; person without civil capacity; harm caused by assisting behavior; spinal cord injury; tort liability; Ji et al. — dispute over liability of educational institution
full_text_en:
Ding v. Ji et al. — Dispute over Educational Institution Liability

Ruling Summary

When, due to the teaching needs of an educational training institution, the guardian of a person without civil capacity is unable to actually perform guardianship duties, the educational training institution shall assume the duties of supervision, management, and protection over such person without civil capacity during such period. If the educational training institution fails to perform the aforesaid duties due to its own reasons, resulting in a person without civil capacity, during the period of study and living at the educational training institution, causing harm to others by performing an act of assistance, and if the person without civil capacity subjectively has no intent to cause harm and objectively lacks the cognitive ability to foresee that the act of assistance might cause harm, the educational training institution shall bear tort liability in accordance with the law.

Plaintiff: Ding, female, born on June 22, 2013, Han Chinese, residing in Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang (mother of the plaintiff Ding), female, born on February 22, 1988, Han Chinese, residing in Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Ji A, female, born on July 6, 2013, Han Chinese, residing in Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Ji B, father of the defendant Ji A.

Defendant: Ji B (father of the defendant Ji A), male, born on July 10, 1988, Han Chinese, residing in Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Wang (mother of the defendant Ji A), female, born on December 22, 1987, Han Chinese, residing in Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Xinghua City Mou Dance Art Training Center, domiciled at: Xinghua City, Jiangsu Province. Legal Representative: Gu.

The plaintiff Ding initiated a civil lawsuit with the Xinghua City People's Court of Jiangsu Province regarding a dispute over educational institution liability with the defendants Ji A, Ji B, Wang, and Xinghua City Mou Dance Art Training Center (hereinafter referred to as Mou Dance Center).

The plaintiff Ding alleged that while receiving dance training at the defendant Mou Dance Center, due to the Mou Dance Center's poor management, the actions of the defendant Ji A caused the plaintiff, who was training, to be injured while performing a backbend. Because the defendants refused to compensate, she filed a lawsuit requesting the court to order: 1. Ji A, Ji B, and Wang to compensate for medical expenses, nursing expenses during hospitalization, post-discharge nursing expenses, mental distress damages, and other losses totaling RMB 2,141,925.6; since the Mou Dance Center has already compensated RMB 515,000, the claim is for RMB 1,626,925.6; expenses incurred after the filing to be claimed separately after actual occurrence; 2. Mou Dance Center to bear joint and several liability.

The defendants Ji A, Ji B, and Wang argued: 1. Ji A had no fault in this incident and should not bear compensation liability. 2. Medical expenses to be determined by the court; no objection to hospital meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, nursing expenses during hospitalization, post-discharge nursing expenses, and disability compensation; mental distress damages, transportation expenses, accommodation expenses, and rehabilitation supplies expenses to be determined by the court at its discretion; no objection to the authenticity of the appraisal fees, but they are not relevant.

The defendant Mou Dance Center argued: 1. Mou Dance Center is a lawfully registered institution; it is a fact that the plaintiff Ding participated in dance training there, but it does not assume guardianship responsibilities. Mou Dance Center required parents to cooperate in managing students and report health conditions, and had instructed students on precautions; there was no fault in management. 2. Parents were fully aware of the risks of participating in dance training; Ding's own physical condition was also different, and Ding's injury was directly caused by the actions of the defendant Ji A; Mou Dance Center should not bear compensation liability. 3. Medical expenses to be reviewed by the court; no objection to hospital meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, nursing expenses during hospitalization, post-discharge nursing expenses, disability compensation, accommodation expenses, rehabilitation supplies expenses, and appraisal fees; mental distress damages to be determined by the court at its discretion; regarding transportation expenses, Mou Dance Center frequently accompanied Ding to medical visits in the early stage and paid for them, and Mou Dance Center has already advanced over RMB 500,000 in expenses.

The Xinghua City People's Court of Jiangsu Province found at first instance:

The defendant Mou Dance Center is a private non-enterprise unit approved and established by the Xinghua City Education Bureau, with a business scope of youth dance art training. The defendant Ji A and the plaintiff Ding began studying children's Chinese dance at Mou Dance Center in February 2017 and May 2017, respectively. On December 15, 2018, at 4:50 p.m., Ding and Ji A attended a dance class at the center, the content of which was basic skills practice for Chinese dance. According to the Mou Dance Center's rules, when students were in class, parents were not allowed to enter the classroom but could watch their children's practice through surveillance video in the waiting area. On the day of the incident, there were 19 students (approximately 5 years old), standing in three rows. The classroom floor was reinforced wood flooring, and each student practiced standing on a yoga mat. The class was taught by one professional dance teacher, Xu (a registered dance teacher of the China Dancers Association). Ding and Ji A stood in the third row, with Ji A to Ding's right. During the second half of the class, the teacher considered that three students (including Ji A) had not yet reached the basic skill level for backbends and were exempted from practicing them, and required the other 16 students to practice the backbend movement. When the teacher asked the students to rise from the backbend, including Ding, some students failed to rise in time. When Ji A, who was standing nearby watching her classmates do backbends, noticed that Ding had not risen in time, she walked over to Ding and pulled up Ding's arms that were supporting her on the floor, causing Ding to fall backward, landing on her back and sitting down on the floor. Ding immediately showed signs of discomfort. At that time, the teacher was helping students in the second row who had not risen in time, with her back to Ding and Ji A, and did not notice the above situation. Shortly after the students practiced the backbend movement, the dance class ended. When Ding's mother entered the classroom to help Ding put on clothes, Ding was crying. That evening, Ding felt pain in her lower limbs. Her parents immediately took her to Xinghua City Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Xinghua City People's Hospital for examination. The next day, she was hospitalized at Nanjing Children's Hospital from December 16, 2018, to December 21, 2018, with a discharge diagnosis of thoracolumbar spinal cord injury. On December 21, 2018, Ding was transferred to Nanjing Zijin Hospital for rehabilitation treatment, hospitalized from December 21, 2018, to February 26, 2019, with a discharge diagnosis of thoracolumbar spinal cord injury. On February 25, 2019, Ding was transferred to Jiangsu Zhongshan Geriatric Rehabilitation Hospital, hospitalized from February 25, 2019, to March 9, 2020, with discharge diagnoses of: (1) spinal cord injury, (2) paraplegia, (3) neurogenic bladder, and (4) neurogenic bowel. During this period, Mou Dance Center also accompanied Ding to hospitals in Shanghai and other places for treatment and paid Ding a total of RMB 526,205.

On April 3, 2020, upon application by the plaintiff Ding, the court commissioned the Judicial Expertise Institute of Jiangsu University to conduct a forensic medical evaluation of the degree of disability, period of lost work, nursing period, nutrition period, nursing dependence, and number of nurses for Ding's injuries. On June 7, 2020, the institute issued Forensic Expertise Opinion No. [2020] Lin Jian Zi 180, with the following opinion: 1. The examinee Ding, due to traumatic thoracolumbar spinal cord injury resulting in paraplegia (lower limb muscle strength grade 1) accompanied by severe defecation dysfunction and severe urination dysfunction, constitutes a Grade I physical disability; 2. The examinee has completely lost the ability to work, so there is no need to evaluate the period of lost work; the recommended nursing period is long-term care, with the recommended number of nurses being one person; the recommended nutrition period is 450 days; 3. The examinee's care level is mostly dependent care.

The Xinghua City People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

The right to health of citizens is protected by law. If a person without civil capacity suffers personal injury during the period of study or living at a kindergarten, school, or other educational institution, and the kindergarten, school, or other educational institution fails to fulfill its education and management duties, it shall bear liability.

The defendant Mou Dance Center is a private institution with a business scope of youth dance art training, and its assumed liability shall be equivalent to the liability of an educational institution under the Tort Liability Law. The plaintiff Ding was born on June 22, 2013, and was a person without civil capacity at the time of the incident. As the dance education manager, Mou Dance Center had the duty to educate, manage, and protect Ding during the period when Ding was studying dance at the center. In particular, Mou Dance Center did not allow parents to enter the classroom for ease of management, which further increased Mou Dance Center's protection duties. From the facts found by the court, although the students in the dance class where Ding and the defendant Ji A were enrolled had mostly undergone over a year of professional training, they were after all persons without civil capacity. The backbend, as a dangerous dance training movement, required an adult to be present to watch and assist when performing it. However, at the time of the incident, Mou Dance Center only provided one professional dance teacher for the 19 young children, making it impossible to ensure that all children were within the teacher's controllable range. When Ji A pulled up Ding's arms that were supporting her on the floor, causing Ding to fall backward and land on her back, the dance teacher failed to discover and stop it in time, leading to the accident. Therefore, Mou Dance Center failed to fulfill its full safety protection obligations, had obvious fault regarding the occurrence of this incident, and should bear corresponding compensation liability.

Although the defendant Ji A is a person without civil capacity and lacks basic cognitive ability regarding danger, her act of pulling up the plaintiff Ding's arms that were supporting her on the floor directly caused the consequence of Ding's injury. Since Ding is a person without civil capacity, the corresponding civil compensation liability shall be borne by Ji A's guardians, the defendants Ji B and Wang.

The plaintiff Ding herself had no subjective fault or negligence regarding her injury. Moreover, before the accident, Ding had been regularly participating in dance training. The defendant Mou Dance Center failed to submit evidence proving that Ding's "occult spina bifida" had a causal relationship with the occurrence of the harmful consequence. Therefore, Ding shall not bear liability according to law.

Considering the degree of fault of each party, it was determined that the defendants Ji A, Ji B, and Wang should bear 10% of the liability for Ding's injury, and the defendant Mou Dance Center should bear 90% of the liability for Ding's injury. The total losses of Ding were determined to be RMB 2,114,847.21. Ji B and Wang were to compensate 10% thereof, i.e., RMB 211,484.7, and Mou Dance Center was to compensate 90% thereof, i.e., RMB 1,903,362.5. After deducting the RMB 526,205 already advanced by Mou Dance Center, an additional RMB 1,377,157.5 was to be paid.

Accordingly, the Xinghua City People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Articles 16, 26, paragraph 1 of Article 32, and Article 38 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 19, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, and 26 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Personal Injury Compensation, and Articles 64 and 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 3, 2020:

1. The defendant Xinghua City Mou Dance Art Training Center shall, within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff Ding for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidies, nursing expenses, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, mental distress damages, transportation expenses, accommodation expenses, expenses for disability assistive devices, and other expenses, totaling RMB 1,377,157.5.

2. The defendants Ji B and Wang shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff Ding for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidies, nursing expenses, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, mental distress damages, transportation expenses, accommodation expenses, expenses for disability assistive devices, and other expenses, totaling RMB 211,484.7.

Ji A, Ji B, Wang, and Mou Dance Center disagreed with the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

Ji A, Ji B, and Wang appealed, arguing: 1. Ji A saw that the appellee Ding had not risen in time after practicing the backbend movement and came forward to assist out of goodwill; this act was a rescue act and had no legal causal relationship with the consequence of injury; Ji A should not bear compensation liability. 2. When practicing the backbend movement, the teacher did not clearly indicate the relevant risks and precautions, nor did she expressly state that students could not help each other; therefore, the appellant Mou Dance Center failed to fulfill its safety management obligations and should bear compensation liability. In summary, they requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment, a remand for retrial, or a revision of the judgment finding that Ji A, Ji B, and Wang should not bear compensation liability.

Mou Dance Center appealed, arguing: 1. Mou Dance Center had performed its management duties diligently during the training and had no fault; bearing 90% liability was excessive. 2. The appellee Ding's injury was directly caused by the spontaneous act of the appellant Ji A; Ji A should have realized that her act could cause Ding to fall and be injured; if Ji A had not come forward to pull up Ding's arms, Ding would not have been injured; therefore, Ji A should bear 20-30% of the compensation liability. 3. The court's decision that Mou Dance Center pay Ding's future nursing expenses (for 20 years) in a lump sum was unreasonable; payment should be made in installments. In summary, they requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment, a remand for retrial, or a revision of the judgment to reduce Mou Dance Center's compensation liability.

Ding responded, arguing: 1. The appellant Ji A should have understood that Ding's act was a rising movement after a backbend and should also have understood that there was a certain danger during the rising process; therefore, Ji A's act of coming forward was itself faulty; there was no so-called rescue act in this case; Ji A should bear compensation liability. 2. The appellant Mou Dance Center had management dereliction regarding Ding's injury; the proportion of liability determined by the court was appropriate. 3. The court's judgment for lump-sum payment did not violate legal provisions and took into account the relevant circumstances of this case. In summary, they requested the dismissal of the appeals and the upholding of the original judgment.

After the second instance, the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province confirmed the facts found at first instance.

During the second instance, the appellants Ji B and Wang voluntarily promised to compensate the appellee Ding RMB 50,000.

The Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at second instance:

The issues in dispute in the second instance were: 1. Who was the subject bearing compensation liability; 2. Whether future nursing expenses should be paid in a lump sum or in installments.

Regarding Issue 1: The subject bearing compensation liability.

The appellant Mou Dance Center is a lawfully registered youth dance training institution. Both the appellant Ji A and the appellee Ding were receiving dance skills training at Mou Dance Center, and both were persons without civil capacity. Therefore, Mou Dance Center owed full duties of supervision, management, and protection over Ji A and Ding, who were undergoing dance training during class hours. In this case, on the day of the incident, Mou Dance Center only provided one professional dance teacher for the 19 students without civil capacity. When Ding was performing the dangerous backbend movement, the dance teacher did not provide waist protection. Ji A's act of pulling up Ding's arms was also not discovered or stopped in time. Mou Dance Center failed to fulfill its duties of education, management, and protection and shall bear compensation liability for Ding's personal injury according to law.

Article 6, paragraph 1 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "An actor who through fault infringes upon another person's civil rights and interests shall bear tort liability." In this case, the "Notice to New Students" submitted by the appellant Mou Dance Center at first instance states: "Except for open classes, during class hours, without the teacher's permission, parents may not enter the classroom, so as not to distract students and affect teaching effectiveness." This regulation made it impossible for the guardians of all minor students to actually perform their guardianship duties during class hours. Both the appellant Ji A and the appellee Ding were under the supervision and management of Mou Dance Center. Ji A, as a classmate of Ding in the dance class, spontaneously came forward to help Ding out of goodwill when Ding had difficulty rising from the backbend. This act was not unlawful. As a person without civil capacity, Ji A subjectively had no intent to harm Ding and objectively lacked the cognitive ability to foresee that her act might cause harm to her classmate Ding. Therefore, Ji A shall not bear compensation liability for Ding's injury according to law. The first-instance court's determination that Ji A and her guardians should bear compensation liability was contrary to law and is corrected.

The guardians of the appellant Ji A, Ji B and Wang, out of deep sympathy for the appellee Ding's injury, voluntarily offered to compensate Ding RMB 50,000 in the second instance. This reflects the traditional virtue of mutual help and fraternity of the Chinese nation. This act is commended and permitted.

In summary, the appellant Mou Dance Center shall bear compensation liability for the appellee Ding's personal injury. Ding's losses total RMB 2,114,847.21. After deducting the RMB 526,205 already advanced by Mou Dance Center, Mou Dance Center shall further pay RMB 1,588,642.21.

Regarding Issue 2: Whether future nursing expenses should be paid in a lump sum or in installments.

Future nursing expenses are generally paid in a lump sum. If lump-sum payment is indeed difficult, payment in installments is permissible, but not mandatory, provided that corresponding security is furnished. In this case, the appellant Mou Dance Center did not provide evidence proving that lump-sum payment was indeed difficult, nor did it provide corresponding security. The first-instance court, after considering the relevant circumstances of this case, ordered lump-sum payment, which complies with legal provisions.

Accordingly, the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Item 2 of paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 27, 2021:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2020) Su 1281 Min Chu No. 1079 of the Xinghua City People's Court of Jiangsu Province;

2. The appellant Xinghua City Mou Dance Art Training Center shall, within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the appellee Ding for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidies, nursing expenses, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, mental distress damages, transportation expenses, accommodation expenses, expenses for disability assistive devices, and other expenses, totaling RMB 1,588,642.21;

3. The appellants Ji B and Wang shall, within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the appellee Ding with RMB 50,000;

4. Dismiss the other claims of the appellee Ding.
